title: CMYK colour lithophane specifications

materials: translucent PLA or PETG in cyan, magenta, yellow, and white
target.backlight: diffuse cool-white LED panel or light box

method.name: stacked subtractive CMYK lithophane
method.principle: White is the light-transmitting base; yellow, magenta, and cyan are translucent colour layers. Their combined thickness controls perceived colour and brightness.

layer_thickness.note: Colour layers can never be thinner than one printed layer (0.08 mm at the PLA layer height).

white.requirements: translucent white, consistent diameter, low yellowing

backlight_tips: Use a diffuse white light source; avoid bare LEDs that create hot spots.
Start with a cool-white backlight around 5000-6500 K.
Keep the backlight evenly spaced behind the print.
Use lower brightness first, then increase gradually to avoid washing out colour.
For a warmer look, try 4000-5000 K; for a cleaner, cooler look, try 6000-6500 K.
Do not use high-power incandescent bulbs near PLA; use LED lighting instead.
Calibrate colour layers with a step wedge before printing a full image.

print_settings.orientation: flat, with the white base closest to the backlight
print_settings.multi_material: Assign each colour to its own AMS/CFS slot and use the slicer’s colour-change workflow.

test_files.purpose: Calibrate layer thickness per colour and measure colour accuracy.
Validate a simple high-contrast photo before a large print.
Check brightness and contrast without colour layers.

acceptance.functional: Produces a recognizable, evenly lit colour image with no major hot spots or colour banding.
acceptance.mechanical: Layers bond securely and the lithophane does not crack during handling.
acceptance.colour: Cyan, magenta, and yellow layers produce visibly distinct colour mixing.

sources.topic: CMYK colour lithophane method and layer guidance
